findings.text: The central packet descriptor begins with polymorphic queue linkage that can serve as doubly linked queue pointers, as a balanced tree node, or as list primitives. Early placement of forward and backward linkage is load bearing for queue head compatibility. Device association shares space with scratch storage for protocol use. Later areas hold socket association, alternative timing representations, a fixed control scratch region, route reference paired with a release callback or an alternate sorted anchor, packet and fragment lengths, header extents, queue selection, single bit state flags, an optional extension count, a grouped header region intended for single copy, and trailing buffer pointers with size accounting and reference count plus optional extension pointer.

Forward linkage at the very start must match the queue head layout or queue operations misinterpret memory. The grouped header region is defined as jointly copied while earlier length and mapping fields and later buffer pointers are excluded from that joint copy. Trailing buffer extent and accounting fields must remain at the end for allocation logic. Movement of the clone indicator requires coordinated update of its mask and position constants.

Clone presence uses an endian sensitive mask with a position constant derived from a zero length marker, packet type limits appear in two spellings for shifted and unshifted use with a position constant from another marker, timestamp kind uses a mask plus shift with ingress marking variants that differ between configurations, and a monochrome classifier offset is exposed from a third marker.

Allocation behaviour selects fast clone, receive path, and poll context through small integer bits, while route reference encoding reserves the low pointer bit to mark absence of an owned reference with a complementary mask preserving the pointer remainder.

A fast clone carrier holds two full packet descriptors plus a shared clone reference count. A sequential walk cursor records lower and upper bounds, fragment position, stepping progress, root and current descriptors, and fragment address with offset. Hash provenance distinguishes absent, link, network, and transport levels.

Creation helpers forward size and allocation context to a common allocator, with one variant requesting paired fast clone storage. A partial copy helper forwards headroom and allocation context while declining clone pairing. Padding ensures a requested tail allowance with failure signalling. Release helpers route to reason aware list release, generic free, or consumption alias.

Route association is read through a masked pointer with a debug check that unowned references occur under read side protection. Helpers allow taking the raw encoded value leaving emptiness, restoring a taken value after verifying emptiness, installing an owned reference while marking slow path state, installing an unowned reference with a protection warning, and testing for live unowned association.

Hash helpers clear all hash state, conditionally clear when transport provenance is absent, install hardware or software provenance with transport flag derivation, copy hash triple between descriptors, and lazily compute on demand returning the stored value. Flow dissection helpers zero the destination keys then delegate to shared dissection with varying scope from full keys to basic keys to symmetric retrieval. Decrypted state helpers compare, test, and copy a conditional flag that collapses to neutral when disabled.

Queue state is inspected through emptiness, lockless emptiness, last and first tests, and safe traversal that prefetches the successor before stepping. Peek variants return the head element, the raw head linkage, the successor of a given element, or the tail element, yielding absence at the sentinel. Removal detaches the generic list node and clears queue membership. Readability reflects an unreadable flag while poisoning and clearing helpers manage debug list state.

Reference handling includes increment with return of the same descriptor, conditional release distinguishing sole ownership with ordering from shared decrement, shared header data release distinguishing sole data ownership with bias for headerless clones, predicates for shared ownership and shared data, expansion of shared headers on demand, sleep allowance when allocation context may block, clone busy detection via paired descriptor ownership and count, plus small predicates for allocator origin, packet type range, poll identifier, and wireless acknowledgement validity.

Buffer extent access supports two layouts where the end is either an offset added to the base or a direct pointer with offset derived by subtraction, plus setters matching each layout. Hardware timestamp access reaches the shared info area. Zero copy state distinguishes pure and managed fragment reference modes, reference acquisition and release through completion callbacks with abort handling, attachment of completion context with flag merging, detachment invoking completion and clearing all zero copy flags, downgrade of managed mode, and datagram iteration from a message iterator.

Unowned route references require read side critical section held in process or bottom half context, enforced by warnings on read and install. Emptiness can be tested locklessly through a single volatile read of the head linkage, and tail peek uses a single volatile read of the tail linkage, while other queue navigation assumes external synchronization.

Hash state starts empty, transitions to populated with software versus hardware origin and transport versus lower level provenance, persists across reads without recomputation when either origin flag is set, downgrades to empty on explicit clear, and copies as a triple of value plus two provenance flags.

A descriptor begins unshared with sole data ownership, may become shared through reference increment or shared data through cloning, returns to exclusive use through cloning for header sharing or full copy for data sharing with release of the old reference, and header release marks header detachment while resetting data sharing count with a shifted bias.

Primary creation enters through size plus allocation context with default placement, and through a fast clone variant that additionally requests paired storage, both serving as the normal ingress for new packet descriptors.

Traversal ingress is provided by head peek and raw head access plus successor and predecessor stepping with boundary failure, and by tail peek for newest element access, forming the supported iteration surface over queue heads.

Stepping past either queue end triggers a fatal check rather than returning garbage. Accessing an unowned route reference outside read side protection risks use after reclaim and is only warned about. Poisoning of list linkage is debug only and absent otherwise, so reliance on poison for correctness is unsafe. Clearing or stealing route state without prior emptiness verification can leak owned references.
The two end representations are mutually exclusive per build: offset form stores a numeric extent while pointer form stores an address, and mixing accessors across forms yields incorrect bounds.
